title: Teluni Implementation Plan
heading: Development handoff qualification
text:
Development handoff qualification
On 2026-11-15 the owner requested synchronizing local development with GitHub before continuing on another computer. The branch and worktree audit found the current optional two-step verification and DataSet increments already published in [PR #40](https://github.com/GabriellMDias/teluni/pull/40); the additional identity-migration worktree was clean and its commit was included. The only local commit outside the published history was the earlier PJ-18 patch, whose remediation was superseded by the source-map override already merged through PR #8. Its original branch is retained on `origin` for history; it does not need to be reapplied.
The PJ-13/PJ-24 qualification correction updates `apps/api/test/identity/pilot-check.ts` to expect the two-step suggestion for a newly provisioned principal and the original destination for a returning person, while asserting that an existing principal ID is preserved. Secure-cookie, private-administration and local/provider session-revocation assertions remain in the rehearsal. Browser journeys also wait for the new branch form's URL-owned `mode=form&record=new` state and derive company workflow URLs from the pathname, preventing dataset search parameters from leaking into cross-module navigation. Browser component files also load sequentially after repeated CI failures importing different test modules before collection; the suite retains all 120 test cases, isolation and timeouts, with three successful cold-cache runs of all 120 tests. All 15 updated module browser journeys also passed locally. Qualification and the final remote gate are tracked in PR #40. The local Docker rehearsal was interrupted because the system partition lacked build space; only cache records created by that attempt were removed. Local tool installations, ignored credentials, media and development databases are machine-local state, outside the source handoff. Follow [setup](../setup.md#persistent-local-environment) to recreate the development services on the other computer; real-environment prerequisites remain in the human-action checklist.
The owner subsequently requested merging PR #40, reviewing every remaining pull request and synchronizing local `main`. PR #40 and the reviewed pnpm action, rate-limit, PostgreSQL and Ubuntu updates were merged. The OpenTelemetry update in PR #33 retains both Fastify updates after resolving their manifest conflict. The PJ-13/PJ-24 follow-up in [PR #43](https://github.com/GabriellMDias/teluni/pull/43) replaces the Dockerfile-only PR #32 and aligns the development/test Keycloak image in `apps/api/scripts/keycloak.ts` with the pilot Dockerfile's updated digest, so identity qualification and deployment use the same provider build. PR #32 was closed after Renovate rewrote its branch and removed the additional qualification changes; the replacement uses a contributor-owned branch. PR #43 includes PR #33's changes for combined qualification; their current-head CI gates must pass before merge. Investigation of an intermediate main CI failure also identified a same-second reauthentication gap in the pinned provider: `max_age=0` alone can reuse the immediately preceding authentication. PR #43 adds `prompt=login` for fresh authentication and a provider-URL regression test, retaining the browser assertions that disabling two-step verification asks for the password and code. These corrections implement the existing identity policy and change no outstanding real-environment prerequisite.

title: Teluni Implementation Plan
heading: PJ-41 interface alignment
text:
PJ-41 interface alignment
The identity board is the visual direction for the product interface: a sidebar on desktop, responsive navigation on smaller screens, a coherent content area, rounded cards and controls, the approved typography and palette, and complete light and dark themes. Adapt its composition to Teluni's real company/branch scopes, permissions and workflows; illustrative menus, copy and imagery do not define new capabilities or require a pixel-for-pixel copy. The [branding guide](branding/README.md) continues to own canonical brand assets and colors.
Recommended priority and delivery sequence:
**Priority foundation, before expanding the next product screens:** inventory the existing shell and shared components; define semantic color, spacing and typography tokens; implement responsive sidebar/header/content structure and accessible light/dark theme selection. Reuse existing components and boundaries. Preserve company/branch context, authorization, routes, session behavior and localized content. Deliver a representative existing workflow in both themes to validate the structure before wider adoption.
**Incremental adoption alongside functional work:** migrate existing identity, organization, device, media, programming, catalog and publication screens to the shared structure. New product screens use that structure once available. Independent API, player, security and operational work can continue; this task does not replace their gates or require rewriting functional modules.
**Final refinement before PJ-14 acceptance:** complete screen coverage, hierarchy, empty/loading/error states and responsive details; compare desktop/mobile screenshots with the board's visual direction. Finish both themes before the pilot usability assessment, rather than deferring the whole interface to the end.
Acceptance requires consistent shared components and both themes across the product panel, keyboard navigation and visible focus, readable contrast, responsive desktop/mobile layouts without unintended horizontal overflow, and regression coverage for existing user journeys and access denials. Record visual comparisons and verification evidence, update affected documentation and generated references, and pass the applicable web checks and full `pnpm validate`. Keycloak pages must remain visually coherent within the provider's boundaries; this task does not redesign the developer documentation portal or the Android player's interface. Theme preference behavior must be specified and tested during implementation.
The owner subsequently authorized continued development and a pull request on 2026-10-23. The first increment implements the responsive sidebar/header/content structure, semantic product colors, localized System/Light/Dark selection, keyboard dismissal and a skip link. Appearance stores only a light/dark preference, follows system changes when unset, synchronizes across tabs and degrades safely if storage is unavailable. The representative workflows are the home page, company entry/forms, denied company access and sign-in. Existing company-specific navigation remains in its workflows; moving it into the sidebar, reviewing every module-specific state, final visual refinement and Keycloak theme alignment remain pending. The developer portal remains separate. No production or pilot gate is changed.
Verification (2026-10-23): frozen install, lint, types, architecture, documentation, provenance and generated API/database/SDK/portal checks passed locally. The web suites passed 72 unit and 91 browser component tests; the five new shell journeys cover both themes, persistence, live system changes, cross-tab synchronization, denied/unavailable storage, mobile disclosure and keyboard focus, viewport overflow and explicit company-access denial, with automated accessibility checks. The focused documentation and shell E2E run passed all 21 journeys. Build, production bundle boundaries and process smoke passed. A separate persistent-development smoke passed real Keycloak login, secure session, home and portal; desktop (1440 px) and mobile (390 px) screenshots in both themes were visually reviewed.
The full `pnpm validate` did **not** pass on this Windows host: unchanged API tests reported 294 passed, 12 failed and 17 skipped. The Keycloak image test compares native backslash paths with Dockerfile slash paths; media-dependent tests receive `MEDIA_STORAGE_FULL` because the host volume is below the unchanged 10% reserve. The full E2E attempt also failed during the existing identity fixture's API startup because its native Windows media path does not satisfy the slash-prefixed configuration schema; that run was stopped after diagnosis and its output retained locally. API/storage/security checks were not changed or disabled. Focused web results do not replace the complete gate; the pull request must report its Linux CI result separately. PJ-41 remains in progress for the adoption and qualification work above.

title: Teluni Implementation Plan
heading: Home workspace refinement
text:
Home workspace refinement
2026-11-15: implemented under PJ-41 at the owner's request to improve the Home page's appearance and usability. A concise workspace header and direct new-company action replace the oversized welcome banner. Up to six company cards offer workflow shortcuts only after loading effective capabilities and, with screen-view permission, a bounded preview of active screens and their server-defined connection state. Partial pages are labeled explicitly, missing state responses remain unknown, and a failed access refetch hides cached shortcuts. The Home preview uses a separate query-key suffix so entering a company still fetches that route's access. Account protection is secondary to daily work; a short guide explains the content-to-screen flow. Shared Button, navigation icons, product tokens and the existing light/dark shell are reused, with private presentation helpers in `workspace`. Initial session unavailability retains the sign-in route; a failed recheck of an already loaded session instead offers recovery without showing cached Home data. No API, dependency or player behavior changes are introduced.
Verification (Linux): frozen installation, type checking and focused lint passed. All 131 web browser tests passed, including 16 Home tests for access revocation, unknown/partial data, retry, suspended companies, bounded requests, direct creation and session recovery. The shell journeys verify keyboard navigation, themes, responsive layout and direct workflow/form links. Actual local data was inspected in Chromium at desktop and mobile sizes in both themes, with four clean axe scans; widths 320/768/820/1024 had no horizontal overflow. The full `pnpm validate` attempt ran in an isolated checkout to preserve an existing nested local worktree whose generated files are picked up by the root formatter: 350 API tests, 75 web unit tests, the static/reference/documentation gates, production build/isolation and process smoke passed. Its first E2E run passed 49 of 51 journeys: the initial-session entry case exposed the behavior corrected above, and portal search recorded `net::ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED`. The unchanged portal-search journey and corrected entry both passed on rerun; the final documentation/shell presentation suite passed all 26 journeys. The complete submitted-head CI gate passed in [run 43755074814](https://github.com/GabriellMDias/teluni/actions/runs/43755074814), and [PR #44](https://github.com/GabriellMDias/teluni/pull/44) was merged as `a7c458d`; broader PJ-41 adoption and pilot prerequisites remain unchanged.

title: Teluni Implementation Plan
heading: Company branding and branch location
text:
Company branding and branch location
2026-11-15: implemented under PJ-03/PJ-41 at the owner's request. Company creation/settings include optional raster-logo admission, preview, replacement and removal, authenticated metadata persistence and server-side PNG validation. Home shows the logo after an authorized company detail read. Company forms omit the legacy time-zone field. Branch forms show a full address and confirmed map point, following the owner's clarified preference. Local GeoNames city search centers a feature-local Leaflet/OpenStreetMap map; the server resolves a unique IANA zone from exact geographic boundaries at the selected coordinates under [ADR-0036](../adr/0036-resolve-branch-time-zones-locally-from-confirmed-map-coordinates.md). Additive migrations preserve existing zones and constrain coordinates/address consistency. Legacy API clients remain compatible until a branch has a map point; subsequent direct zone overrides are rejected. Address text and zone lookup stay on Teluni, while map tiles use attribution and normal browser caching. There is no external geocoding account or credential prerequisite.
Verification (Linux): frozen install, focused lint and type checks, 53 organizations API tests, 52 organizations/Home browser tests, and three real-identity organization journeys qualify logo persistence/removal, hostile images, geographic lookup, legacy preservation, tenant isolation, version conflicts, map confirmation, and full draft cancellation. Four desktop/mobile light/dark axe scans had no violations or horizontal overflow. Archived branch forms remain keyboard-scrollable. The complete submitted-head CI gate is the authority for remote qualification; broader PJ-03/PJ-41 and pilot prerequisites retain their existing statuses.
At the owner's additional request, all four existing local test companies received distinct demonstration logos and all ten existing branches received clearly marked demonstration full addresses and confirmed coordinates. API read-back verified every logo/location and preservation of all ten scheduling zones. Names, media, playlists, screens and programming were preserved. This is persistent local test data, separate from source control; a private pre-change metadata backup was retained locally.

title: Teluni Implementation Plan
heading: Screen information architecture
text:

title: Teluni Implementation Plan
heading: Companies dataset grid increment
text:
Companies dataset grid increment
On 2026-10-27 the owner asked for configurable multiple selection in `DataSet` (not offered on the companies page), selection shown only by a light color instead of a radio, subtle lines between header and body cells, resizable columns, sorting by clicking a header, a header options icon on hover with "Ordem Crescente", "Ordem Decrescente" and "Filtrar", and a value filter with search, select-all and one or more values. The grid and the filter list had to stay fast with very many rows, using the best available technology and reusing components.
[ADR-0034](../adr/0034-build-data-grids-on-tanstack-table-and-tanstack-virtual.md) selects headless TanStack Table v9 and TanStack Virtual v3. A new shared `DataGrid` in `apps/web/src/data-grid.tsx` renders only the rows in view with ARIA grid roles, row counts and indexes; rows form one tab stop with arrow, Page, Home/End, Enter and Space keys, and `multiple` adds Ctrl/⌘ and Shift selection and Ctrl/⌘+A. Headers sort on click, expose `aria-sort`, show a filter icon while filtered, and resize by dragging, double-click reset or arrow keys on a labeled separator. The filter lists each column's values under the other columns' filters; with a search, Apply keeps only the chosen values found, and choosing every value removes the filter. A live status shows shown, total and selected counts, and a filter that leaves no row offers Clear filters. `DataSet` composes it, keeps sorting, filters and widths while switching to the form, and derives previous/next from the order shown, so `onPrevious`, `onNext` and `rowName` were removed.
New shared components, each with catalog metadata and a live example: `Checkbox` (native input with a mixed state), `Popover` (native popover attribute in the top layer, anchored, focus return), `Menu` (labeled trigger and keyboard menu), `MultiSelectList` (virtualized, accent-insensitive search, select-all, listbox with active descendant) and `DataGrid`. `Button`, `TextField` and `Checkbox` moved to `controls.tsx` so composed components can use them without an import cycle; `components.tsx` still exports them. The `--ui-color-divider` token maps to Teluni's border color. The companies page uses single selection with sortable, filterable name and access columns; sorting and filtering cover the loaded page, and server-side processing is not provided. No API, schema or permission changes.
The owner then asked for exports to Excel and PDF, leaving other formats to the agent. [ADR-0035](../adr/0035-export-grid-data-in-the-browser-to-xlsx-csv-and-pdf.md) adds Excel (.xlsx), CSV and PDF, offered only where a screen passes `exportName`: an Exportar menu in the DataSet toolbar or the DataGrid footer saves the rows shown, in their order and with their filters, and the columns that have a value. Excel keeps numbers numeric with a bold, frozen header and the widths shown; CSV is UTF-8 with a byte order mark, `;` separators and decimal commas in Portuguese, and guards text that spreadsheets would run as formulas; PDF is A4 with a title, generation time, record count and page numbers. `write-excel-file`, `jsPDF` and `jspdf-autotable` load only when someone exports; core-js's install script, an optional jsPDF dependency, stays disabled. The companies page exports as "Empresas". Unit tests cover the CSV rules and a browser test saves all three formats from a sorted grid.
Local validation on 2026-10-27 on Windows: format, lint, type, architecture, documentation and reference checks passed; web unit (75) and browser component tests (120) passed; the build, bundle checks and API smoke passed; 35 end-to-end journeys passed, including the shell, company navigation and portal journeys. Failures outside this change, in files it does not touch: `deployment:test` joins two absolute Windows paths; 14 API tests (media processing, the Keycloak image and integration cases that create media) failed; and the 7 journeys that start the local API stack, including the companies journey with its new export step, stopped when the API rejected its configuration at startup, with 8 dependent journeys not run. The companies dataset is covered by browser tests against a simulated API. No remote CI result is claimed.

heading: Status and scope
text:
Status and scope
**Approved detailed design for D-13, 2026-10-18.** The owner approved all ten [decisions for review](#decisions-for-review) as proposed, including ADR-0026, under [PH-21](human-actions.md#ph-21), and asked for implementation. Approval authorizes implementation in local and CI environments with synthetic addresses and Mailpit; [implementation status](#implementation-status) records what exists. It specifies company invitations (the selected invitation policy and IA-02) on top of the approved [tenant data design](tenant-data-design.md) and [identity and session design](identity-session-design.md), and the durable transactional-email mechanism they need, whose architectural direction [ADR-0026](../adr/0026-propose-a-postgresql-outbox-and-smtp-relay-for-transactional-email.md) proposes. The approved decisions are listed under [decisions for review](#decisions-for-review).
In scope: who may invite whom and with which access, the invitation lifecycle, the invitation credential and link, acceptance by a verified identity, revalidation, abuse limits, the outbound-mail outbox and dispatcher, SMTP delivery, failure handling, retention, observability and verification. Out of scope: account registration, email verification and password recovery, which Keycloak performs under D-02 and PJ-24; Keycloak's own mail delivery (see [Keycloak mail](#keycloak-mail)); choosing the real mail provider, sender domain and DNS authentication, which remain [PH-17](human-actions.md#ph-17); and legal retention periods, which remain [PH-13](human-actions.md#ph-13).

title: Teluni Company Invitation and Durable Email Delivery Design
heading: Policy inputs
text:
Policy inputs
The design applies these selected policies without changing them:
Company invitations are recipient-bound, single-use, revocable and valid for seven days; a resend invalidates the previous pending invitation; acceptance requires the matching authenticated identity and explicit membership confirmation; changing the recipient requires a new invitation ([identity and access](identity-and-access.md#enrollment-and-account-continuity)).
Email verification establishes mailbox control, not legal identity or company ownership, and accounts are never merged solely by equal email.
Company administrators invite with company scope; branch managers invite operators to their own branches without granting authority beyond their own ([permission matrix](identity-and-access.md#permission-model-and-default-matrix)). New administrators require the responsible administrator's approval (P10) with an authentication no older than five minutes (P14). Temporary access expires explicitly and is never renewed automatically (P30).
Credentials in URLs are allowed only as short-lived, high-entropy, single-purpose values whose exposure is understood; reset and invitation links are `RESTRICTED` ([authentication policy](../security/authentication.md)). Retry, duplicate request, delivery failure and expiry must stay safe for email-based flows.
A durable required side effect records its intent in the same transaction as the change, and consumers tolerate duplicates ([delivery policy](../architecture/delivery-and-side-effects.md)).

title: Teluni Company Invitation and Durable Email Delivery Design
heading: Who may invite
text:
Who may invite
An invitation carries exactly one grant request with the same shape as a direct grant: a standard role, either the whole company or one to 100 explicit active branches of the company, and an optional grant expiry. The rules mirror direct grants:
Inviter
May invite
Conditions
Company administrator
Operator or branch manager, company-wide or for any active branches
Company active
Responsible administrator
Additionally company administrator, always company-wide
An authentication no older than five minutes; the invitation is the P10 approval
Branch manager
Operator only, for a subset of the branches the manager currently manages
Never company-wide, never another role
Operator
Nobody
—
A new capability, `invitations.manage`, is company-wide for administrators and branch-scoped for managers. Administrators see and manage every invitation of the company; a branch manager sees and manages only invitations whose whole branch scope lies inside the branches they currently manage. Invitation lists are paginated and cursor-bound like other company lists.
At invitation time the system never looks up principals by email: it neither reveals whether the address belongs to an account or a member nor links anything by address. The address binds only the later acceptance.

title: Teluni Company Invitation and Durable Email Delivery Design
heading: Invitation lifecycle
text:
Invitation lifecycle
PENDING ──accept──▶ ACCEPTED
   │ ├──revoke──▶ REVOKED
   │ ├──resend──▶ REPLACED   (a new PENDING invitation takes its place)
   │ └──7 days──▶ EXPIRED    (recorded lazily; an expired row is never accepted)

**Create.** Validates the recipient address (trimmed, at most 254 characters, one `@`, compared in lower case) and the grant request, then inserts the invitation, enqueues its email in the same transaction and writes one `invitation.created` audit event. A company has at most one pending invitation per normalized address (a partial unique index); creating another returns `INVITATION_PENDING`, and the panel offers resend instead.
**Resend.** Marks the pending invitation `REPLACED`, cancels its unsent email, and creates a new invitation with a new credential and a new seven-day validity, in one transaction. The old link stops working immediately.
**Revoke.** Marks the pending invitation `REVOKED` and cancels its unsent email. Revoking a final invitation is a no-op.
**Expire.** Validity ends seven days after creation. Reads treat an expired pending row as expired, and every invitation write in the company first records its expired pending rows as `EXPIRED`, so a new invitation to the same address is never blocked by an expired one and no scheduled job is needed for correctness.
**Accept.** See [acceptance](#acceptance). Acceptance is idempotent for the principal that accepted: repeating it returns the same result, so a lost response can be retried safely.
Every change writes its audit event in the same transaction. Audit details are allowlisted (invitation ID, role, scope, branch count, grant expiry, replaced invitation ID) and never contain the recipient address, so later erasure of the address does not require editing append-only audit rows.
Authority-changing writes follow tenant data design rule 5: the company row is locked first, then the invitation row, then the involved membership rows in ID order, and the actor's current access is rechecked inside the transaction.

title: Teluni Company Invitation and Durable Email Delivery Design
heading: Invitation credential and link
text:
Invitation credential and link
**Credential.** 32 bytes from the platform CSPRNG, encoded base64url. The invitation stores only its SHA-256 hash, under a unique index used for lookup. The credential is `RESTRICTED`: it never appears in logs, telemetry, errors, audit, analytics, query strings or the panel after acceptance.
**Delivery copy.** The email must contain the credential, so the outbox row keeps it encrypted with authenticated encryption under a dedicated outbound-mail key ring (key ID stored with the ciphertext, newest key first, older keys readable during rotation). The ciphertext is erased when the message reaches a final state (sent, failed or cancelled). After that, the credential is not recoverable from the database; a lost email is handled by resending, which issues a new credential.
**Link.** `{public origin}/invitations/accept#{credential}`. The fragment is never sent in HTTP requests or `Referer` headers. The panel reads it, keeps it in the tab's `sessionStorage`, removes it from the address bar with `history.replaceState`, and sends it only in the body of `POST` requests. Sign-in returns to `/invitations/accept` without the credential, and the panel resumes from `sessionStorage`; the stored value is cleared after acceptance, after a final error or when the tab closes.

title: Teluni Company Invitation and Durable Email Delivery Design
heading: Acceptance
text:
Acceptance
The invitee opens the link. Without a session, the page explains the invitation and offers sign-in through the existing login flow. Account registration, if the invitee has no account, is D-02's signup flow and is not designed here; until it exists, only people with an existing verified account can accept.
With a session, the panel calls a preview operation with the credential. It answers with the company display name, the role, the scope (branch names), any grant expiry, the invitation expiry and the inviter's display name, or with a failure. A preview has no effect.
The invitee explicitly confirms. The accept operation then, in one transaction:
finds the invitation by credential hash and locks its company row, the invitation row and the involved membership rows in that order; an unknown credential answers `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, and a final or expired one `INVITATION_NO_LONGER_VALID`;
requires that the session principal's verified email (identity's snapshot from the latest verified sign-in; sign-in already rejects unverified addresses) equals the recipient address case-insensitively, otherwise `INVITATION_RECIPIENT_MISMATCH`, which never reveals the invited address;
revalidates the invitation against current state: the company is active; the inviter is still an active member who could grant this role and scope now (for an administrator invitation, still the responsible administrator; for a manager's invitation, still managing every branch); every branch is still active. If anything fails, the invitation becomes invalid with `INVITATION_NO_LONGER_VALID` rather than being narrowed silently, and the inviter can issue a new one;
applies the membership rule below, inserts the grant with the inviter as grantor, marks the invitation `ACCEPTED`, and writes one `invitation.accepted` audit event.
Invitee's membership in the company
Result
None
A new active membership with the invited grant
Active
The invited grant is added to the existing membership (an identical effective grant is not duplicated)
Suspended
Refused with `MEMBERSHIP_SUSPENDED`; suspension is lifted only by an administrator, never by an invitation
Removed
A new active membership; the removed membership stays as history. The membership uniqueness rule becomes `UNIQUE (company_id, principal_id) WHERE status <> 'REMOVED'`
Since the 2026-10-28 revision, no invited role requires two-step verification at use.

title: Teluni Company Invitation and Durable Email Delivery Design
heading: Durable email delivery
text:
Durable email delivery
[ADR-0026](../adr/0026-propose-a-postgresql-outbox-and-smtp-relay-for-transactional-email.md) sets the direction; this section specifies it.
**Ownership.** A new API module, `mail`, owns an `outbound_emails` table, the dispatcher and the SMTP adapter. It is platform-operational infrastructure without its own business meaning: producers own what a message means. Its public port lets a producer enqueue a message with a template key, locale, recipient, allowlisted parameters and an optional secret parameter inside the producer's own database transaction, and cancel a message it enqueued. Organizations is the first producer. The table has no tenant key because future producers (identity notices, platform messages) are not tenant-scoped; each row records its producer and producer reference, and invitation rows reference their message.
**Message states.** `PENDING` (waiting for a first or later attempt), `SENT`, `FAILED` (attempts exhausted or permanent rejection) and `CANCELLED` (cancelled by the producer before sending). A row records attempts, next attempt time, lease expiry, last failure class and the SMTP reply code, never the raw provider text or the message body.
**Dispatcher.** Runs inside the API process when the mail settings are configured, started after the server is ready and stopped during drain. Every few seconds, or when signalled after a commit in the same process, it claims a small batch with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`: due `PENDING` rows whose lease is absent or expired, setting a lease of two minutes and incrementing attempts. Several API instances can run it safely; the pilot runs one. For each message it decrypts the secret parameter, renders the templates and submits through SMTP with connection and total timeouts of 30 seconds. Shutdown stops claiming, lets in-flight sends finish within the drain deadline, and leaves the rest to lease expiry.
**Outcomes and retries.**
SMTP outcome
Result
Accepted (2xx after `DATA`)
`SENT`, secret erased
Permanent rejection (5xx)
`FAILED` immediately, secret erased
Transient failure (4xx, connection, TLS or timeout)
Retry after about 1, 5, 15 and 60 minutes, then 3, 6 and 12 hours, with jitter; `FAILED` after the 8th attempt (about 22 hours, well inside the seven-day invitation)
Retries use the same `Message-ID`, derived from the message ID, so mail clients can recognize repeats. Delivery is at least once: a crash after the relay accepted a message but before `SENT` was recorded sends it again when the lease expires. A duplicate invitation email carries the same still-valid link, so the duplicate is harmless. Bounces after acceptance by the relay and provider webhooks are not handled in this version; the panel shows "sent" as "handed to the mail service", not as delivered.
**Panel feedback.** The invitation list shows each pending invitation's delivery state (waiting, sent, or failed) and offers resend and revoke. A failed delivery never silently disappears.
**Failure windows.** Committing the invitation and its message together closes the commit/publication gap. The relay-accepted/not-recorded gap is the accepted duplicate above. A revoke racing an in-flight send can deliver a link that no longer works, which acceptance rejects. Losing the database after `SENT` loses nothing a resend cannot recreate.
**Transport.** SMTP submission with authentication through the established `nodemailer` library, pinned like other dependencies. Production requires implicit TLS or mandatory STARTTLS with certificate verification; plaintext SMTP is accepted only for loopback or test sinks outside production. The relay is provider-neutral, so PH-17 can choose any service that offers authenticated SMTP submission, and changing provider is a configuration change.
**Configuration concepts.** Relay host and port, TLS mode, username, password (`RESTRICTED`), sender address and display name, and the outbound-mail key ring (`RESTRICTED`). Names are added to the canonical configuration schema when implemented. Like other module requirements, mail stays unmounted outside production until configured, and production refuses to start when a module that requires mail is composed without it. Invitations require mail.
**Observability.** Metrics: messages by state, age of the oldest due `PENDING` message, attempts, send latency, and failures by class. Logs and traces carry message, producer and invitation IDs, never recipient addresses, credentials or bodies. Alert thresholds and channels remain D-09; until then, the oldest pending age and failure counts are visible through metrics.

Keycloak mail
Keycloak sends its own verification and recovery email synchronously, through the SMTP settings the realm provisioning script writes, and the person can request it again. Teluni configures Keycloak with the same relay and sender. Those messages do not pass through the outbox, and their durability remains Keycloak's behavior, qualified under PJ-24.

heading: Verification
text:
Verification
Integration tests against migrated PostgreSQL, the synthetic two-company fixture and a disposable Mailpit:
IA-02: the verified recipient accepts once within seven days; a wrong recipient, replay by another principal, and revoked, replaced or expired invitations fail; a repeated acceptance by the same principal returns the same result; no account is linked by email.
Inviter scope: managers cannot invite beyond operators or outside their branches; non-responsible administrators cannot invite administrators; stale assurance is rejected; cross-company identifiers answer not found.
Revalidation: acceptance fails after the inviter loses authority or responsibility, after a branch is archived and after company suspension; nothing is narrowed silently.
Membership cases: none, active, suspended and removed, with the partial uniqueness rule.
Atomicity: a failed invitation insert enqueues no message; revoke and resend cancel unsent messages; audit events commit exactly once.
Delivery: Mailpit receives the rendered `pt-BR` and `en-US` messages with a working link; injected 4xx, 5xx, timeout and crash-after-accept cases follow the retry table; competing dispatchers never send one claim twice; secrets are erased at final states; no address or credential appears in captured logs.
Limits and retention: the per-company, pending and per-address limits; cleanup removes rows on schedule.
A browser journey sends an invitation, reads the message from Mailpit, signs in as the recipient, accepts and sees the company; a second identity with a different address is refused.

title: Teluni Company Invitation and Durable Email Delivery Design
heading: Decisions for review
text:
Decisions for review
The owner approved each item as proposed on 2026-10-18 under [PH-21](human-actions.md#ph-21):
**Delivery architecture (ADR-0026).** Application-owned transactional email through a PostgreSQL outbox written in the producer's transaction, an in-process dispatcher in the API, and a provider-neutral authenticated SMTP relay through `nodemailer`; no message broker, separate worker service, provider HTTP API or webhook in this version.
**Delivery guarantees.** At least once, with possible duplicates after a crash; up to eight attempts over about 22 hours, immediate failure on permanent rejection, and failures shown to the inviter, who can resend.
**Invitation credential.** 256-bit random credential, stored only as a hash; an encrypted copy for delivery under a dedicated key ring, erased at the message's final state; link credential in the URL fragment, removed from the address bar and kept in the tab's session storage during sign-in.
**Acceptance identity.** The session principal's verified email must equal the recipient address case-insensitively, with explicit confirmation; principals are never looked up by email at invitation time; until D-02 signup exists, only people with an existing verified account can accept.
**Membership cases.** An active member gains the invited grant; a suspended member is refused; a removed person returns as a new membership, which changes membership uniqueness to exclude removed memberships.
**Revalidation at acceptance.** The inviter must still be able to grant the invited role and scope, the company and every branch must be active; otherwise the invitation becomes invalid rather than narrowed. A responsibility transfer therefore invalidates the former responsible administrator's pending administrator invitations.
**Who invites.** Administrators invite operators and branch managers; only the responsible administrator, with a five-minute recent authentication, invites administrators; branch managers invite operators within their own branches; invitations can carry a grant expiry; one pending invitation per company and address, and resend replaces it.
**Abuse limits and content.** 50 invitations per company per 24 hours, 100 pending per company, 3 invitation emails per address per 24 hours across Teluni; no free-text message; fixed `pt-BR`/`en-US` templates in the company's default locale.
**Retention (provisional until PH-13).** Encrypted credential erased at final state; outbound message rows deleted 30 days after their final state; invitation recipient addresses replaced by a tombstone 90 days after the invitation becomes final; audit events never store the address.
**Keycloak mail.** Keycloak keeps sending its own verification and recovery mail synchronously through the same relay, outside the outbox.
Approving these items authorizes implementation in local and CI environments with synthetic addresses and Mailpit. It does not choose the real mail provider or sender domain (PH-17), set legal retention (PH-13) or authorize sending to real people.

Explicit QR/weather/RSS previews use the authenticated API; unavailable sources do not discard the draft. Clock previews show the browser's time, while playback follows each screen's configured location.
A widget is `kind: "widget"` with a version 1 `widget` configuration. Common properties are `locale` (`pt-BR`/`en-US`), `textSize` (24–200 canvas units) and `foreground` (`#RRGGBB`). Existing area background and geometry still apply. QR areas require at least 240 × 240 canvas units to retain a usable code and quiet zone. Widgets are muted at volume zero and cannot participate in coordinated layout pages. Their output defaults to their configured presentation (`{ "view": true }`); an active regional playlist rule can override it. Switching an existing playlist default to a widget follows the same explicit default-removal confirmation as a catalog area.

title: Layout Information Components
heading: Dynamic QR lifecycle
text:
Dynamic QR lifecycle
The opaque link identity is the first 128 bits of SHA-256 over `teluni.qr.v1:<lowercase layout UUID>:<area key>`. Its encoded address is `/q/<identity>` at the configured `TELUNI_PUBLIC_ORIGIN`. The generated matrix is part of the immutable publication. No external QR image service or Android encoder dependency is used.
Only a successful manual publication or restore transaction activates the destination through the Programming port. Manual publication inserts or updates the stable link; restore updates an existing identity only and rejects a generation whose source layout/link has been deleted. The repository locks QR rows in identifier order for restore and cascading layout deletion, avoiding reverse layout/program lock acquisition. Drafts and automatic catalog price publications do not advance it. Every use of the same layout area shares its most recently explicitly published destination, including previously displayed copies of the code. Restoring deliberately restores that destination; a publication that is unchanged creates no new generation. Recreating the area with a different key/layout creates a different link. Deleting the layout cascades its links; a suspended company has no public resolution.
The public panel route resolves the current destination through `GET /q/{linkId}`, then navigates. It needs no human session and reveals only the approved public HTTPS destination. The link grants no tenant/API authority. A deployed panel origin must be reachable by scanning devices; localhost links serve local testing only.

title: Layout Information Components
heading: Live sources and cache bounds
text:
Live sources and cache bounds
The API alone fetches providers. Weather uses [MET Norway Locationforecast](https://api.met.no/weatherapi/locationforecast/2.0/documentation), identifies Teluni by User-Agent, credits [MET Norway / CC BY 4.0](https://api.met.no/doc/License), and caches identical coordinates for at least three hours, respecting later provider expiry up to the 24-hour cap. This initial provider needs no API key. RSS/Atom sources cache for at least 15 minutes. Failures have a one-minute retry cooldown. In-flight requests for the same source coalesce; one process holds at most 256 source entries and four concurrent fetches. A busy cache returns unavailable rather than opening unbounded work. Cache misses after an API restart fetch again.
Outbound sources require HTTPS, the standard port, no credentials, control characters or fragments. Every DNS answer must be public; connections pin a validated address while retaining TLS hostname/certificate verification. Every redirect is revalidated, with at most three redirects. Requests have a five-second total deadline, a two-second DNS wait, identity encoding and a 512 KiB body cap. XML refuses DTD/entity declarations, validates structure and enforces at most 32 simultaneously open elements through the parser’s own nesting limit, including quoted attributes and Unicode element names. Only bounded plain text, source labels and validated HTTPS article links cross the API boundary. No source bodies/URLs or arbitrary provider errors are logged.
`POST /companies/{companyId}/programming/widgets/preview` requires a human session, CSRF and `programming.edit` over the selected layout branch (company-wide for a company layout). `GET /device/publications/{publicationId}/widgets` uses credential-aware device limits and serves only the current desired publication; source configuration comes from its stored manifest, never device input. Refreshes do not create new publication generations. Device sidecars omit article URLs (`null`) because screens display headlines without following links; authenticated previews retain the validated links. Even twelve feeds with twenty 200-code-point headlines and 120-code-point source labels stay within the player’s 256 KiB response limit and three-generation 768 KiB cache limit. Player text bounds count Unicode code points consistently with the API.

title: Layout Information Components
heading: Player compatibility and offline behavior
text:
Player compatibility and offline behavior
Widget layouts publish protocol 3. Protocols 1/2 retain exact serialized content and remain supported. Install player version code 3 (`0.1.2`) before assigning widget publications. Older players report incompatibility and retain only still-authorized cached output. Apply the additive `20261116000000_layout_widgets` and `20261116010000_layout_widget_tenant_key` migrations and runtime grants before the new API/player. The second migration adds the explicit tenant-qualified key without rewriting the already applied first migration.
The portable core validates all configuration and live data, derives text/item selection, and applies the existing statement/trusted-clock gate before composing output. Native Android views draw text and QR modules without WebView. Updating a clock or forecast does not restart unrelated media or ticker animation. A generation-specific `widgets.json` cache uses AtomicFiles, preserves at most three generations, and is erased with the identity. It is an independent versioned record, so existing credential/state formats remain readable.
After activation and successful sync, live data refresh at most every 15 minutes, retrying failed transport and stale/unavailable sources after one minute. A newly activated generation refreshes immediately, independently of the previous generation’s interval. Freshness follows `validUntil`; source failures retain clearly stale data only until 24 hours after `fetchedAt`. Missing/expired data show an unavailable placeholder and report degraded playback while other authorized content continues. Caches never extend authorization or turn the device clock into trusted time.

title: Layout Information Components
heading: Verification and local examples
text:
Verification and local examples
API checks cover all variants, export versions, QR decoding/stability and publish-only activation, device/tenant boundaries, canonical protocol bytes, bounded cache expiry, RSS/Atom parsing and pinned public networking including redirect/private-address rejection. Shared API-generated protocol 3 fixtures contain every type and are consumed by JVM parser/planner/cache tests. Existing protocol 1/2, catalog, schedule and player checks remain in the same gate. Browser checks configure/save all five variants and preserve drafts when a source is unavailable.
The local Café Aurora demo contains “Painel informativo · Componentes · Horizontal” and “Recepção conectada · Componentes · Vertical”, both using all five components. The horizontal example is assigned to the demo Android emulator through its own programming group. The example news source is the [React release Atom feed](https://github.com/react/react/releases.atom), displaying headline/source text only; its QR destination is the corresponding public release page. Verification includes publication-activated destination changes without changing the QR matrix. External sources may be unavailable; local verification is not a provider SLA or physical-player qualification.

title: Teluni Media Library Design
heading: Status and scope
text:
Status and scope
**Approved detailed design for D-05, 2026-10-19.** The owner approved all nine [decisions for review](#decisions-for-review) as proposed under [PH-23](human-actions.md#ph-23), including ADR-0028, after asking for development to continue autonomously. Approval authorizes implementation of PJ-09 in local and CI environments with generated fixtures.
In scope: tenant-owned media assets and their branch scope, upload, trustworthy inspection and validation against AT-02/AT-03, the playback rendition profile and conversion (FR-04), processing isolation, private storage and delivery to the panel, archive, trash and reference-safe purge (AT-17), permissions, abuse limits, audit, data, contracts, panel workflow and verification.
Out of scope, with their owners: delivery of renditions to devices inside publications (D-04, PJ-11); playlists and other references to media (PJ-10, PJ-20, PJ-21), which register through the reference port defined here; commercial original-media quotas and the 80%/100% warnings (PJ-27); qualifying any device decoder, memory or storage profile (PH-08, PJ-12); malware scanning and content moderation (pending risk decision, PH-13); the production container image that ships FFmpeg (PJ-13).

title: Teluni Media Library Design
heading: Policy inputs
text:
Policy inputs
The design applies these selected policies without changing them:
Validate declared and inspected type, size, decoded dimensions, duration, compatibility and scoped references; enforce all bounds, not only compressed size: images at most 20 MiB, each decoded axis at most 8,192 px and at most 32,000,000 pixels (AT-02); videos at most 1 GiB and 60 minutes (AT-03). Ingestion bounds are configurable engineering defaults, not plan quotas.
Preserve originals and create compatible renditions when validated processing is supported; show preparation, progress and preview; reject with an actionable reason when safe conversion is unavailable; never silently distort content ([media lifecycle](release-policies.md#media-and-deletion-lifecycle)).
Archiving removes media from new selections without breaking references. Physical deletion is blocked while drafts, active, staged or recovery generations or protected publications reference the media, disclosing only references the caller may see; a recoverable archive or trash lasts at least 30 days before purge (AT-17).
Uploading media is allowed to administrators company-wide and to branch managers and operators in their branches; archive and restore to administrators and branch managers; permanent deletion only to administrators ([permission matrix](identity-and-access.md#permission-model-and-default-matrix)). Share media explicitly with branches or the whole company and enforce scope on lists, previews and downloads, not only on buttons.
Customer media is `CONFIDENTIAL`, private, never public because it appears on a screen, and never addressed by a public filesystem path or a permanent bearer URL ([operations](operations.md#persistent-state-and-storage-portability)). Uploads are not executable content; parsers run isolated ([security requirements](security-and-i18n.md#media-and-audit-protections)).
Media storage is a media-owned capability with replaceable filesystem I/O so that an S3-compatible store can be added later (ADR-0021).

title: Teluni Media Library Design
heading: Assets, scope and visibility
text:
Assets, scope and visibility
An **asset** is one uploaded file and what Teluni derived from it. It belongs to one company and has an owning scope:
**Company** (`branch_id` empty): created by people with company-wide upload authority. Every member with `media.view` anywhere in the company can see and use it; this is the "shared with the whole company" case.
**Branch**: created for one branch. Members with `media.view` on that branch see and use it; others do not learn it exists (`RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`).
Explicit sharing of a branch asset with further selected branches is a later increment of this design (a `media_asset_shares` table with read/use authority only); until then a company-scoped asset is the way to share. Editing authority always follows the owning scope.
Each asset has a name (1 to 120 characters, the uploaded file name by default, never used as a path), a kind (`IMAGE` or `VIDEO`), an optional set of up to 10 tags (each 1 to 40 characters) for organization and search, and the inspected facts: content type, size, width, height, duration and whether it has audio.
